unit: Unit 1: Database System Concepts, ER Model & Relational Design

questions.stem: Which component of the DBMS Storage Manager is responsible for loading disk blocks into main memory frames and implementing cache eviction policies?

options.text: Query Compiler — it generates optimized relational algebra execution plans
Buffer Manager — it allocates RAM frames and flushes dirty pages using algorithms like LRU
Data Dictionary — it computes mathematical joins across non-indexed attributes

questions.rationale: The Buffer Manager is the core subsystem of the storage manager that interfaces with secondary storage to cache disk blocks in main memory and maintain page replacement policies. (Key Takeaway: The Buffer Manager controls memory caching and page replacement.)

questions.stem: In an ER diagram, Total Participation of an entity set in a relationship set is visually denoted by a double line, indicating that every entity in the set must participate in at least one relationship instance.
questions.rationale: True. Total participation (existence dependency) enforces a minimum cardinality of 1 and is drawn with a double line connecting the entity set rectangle to the relationship diamond. (Key Takeaway: Total participation is represented by a double line and indicates existence dependency.)

questions.module_title: Advanced ER and Extended ER (EER) Concepts
questions.stem: In Extended ER (EER) modeling, what does the Disjoint constraint ('d') specify regarding subclass membership?

options.text: An entity instance can belong to multiple subclasses within the specialization simultaneously
An entity instance can be a member of at most one subclass within the specialization
Subclasses are forbidden from inheriting attributes from the parent superclass

questions.rationale: The disjoint constraint ('d') enforces mutual exclusivity among subclasses: an entity can belong to at most one subclass. In contrast, overlapping ('o') permits simultaneous membership in multiple subclasses. (Key Takeaway: Disjoint specialization enforces mutual exclusivity among subclasses.)

questions.stem: When a foreign key is declared with ON DELETE CASCADE, will deleting a record in the parent table automatically delete all matching referencing records in the child table?
questions.rationale: Yes. ON DELETE CASCADE ensures referential integrity by automatically propagating parent record deletions down to referencing child records, preventing orphaned foreign key references. (Key Takeaway: ON DELETE CASCADE automatically deletes associated child records.)

questions.stem: When mapping a 1:N Binary Relationship Set into relations, where should the Foreign Key be placed to ensure single-valued attributes without creating unnecessary extra tables?

options.text: In the '1'-side relation — embed an array of primary keys from the 'N'-side relation
In the 'N'-side relation — embed the primary key of the '1'-side relation as a foreign key attribute
In an auxiliary bridge table — a separate third relation is mandatory for every binary relationship

questions.rationale: In a 1:N relationship (e.g., Department to Employee), each entity on the 'N'-side is associated with at most one entity on the '1'-side. Embedding Dept_ID inside Employee guarantees an atomic single-valued foreign key without null proliferation. (Key Takeaway: In 1:N mappings, embed the foreign key on the 'N'-side relation.)

questions.stem: In Relational Algebra, the Selection operator ($\sigma$) filters columns vertically, while the Projection operator ($\pi$) filters tuples horizontally.
questions.rationale: False — swapped_term. Selection ($\sigma$) filters tuples (rows) horizontally based on a condition, whereas Projection ($\pi$) selects specified attributes (columns) vertically and eliminates duplicates. (Key Takeaway: Selection filters rows horizontally; Projection filters columns vertically.)
